name: Rspamd
description: Spam filtering with private HTTP scanning and milter workers, persistent state, and a password-protected controller UI. Features such as greylisting and rate limits require an external Redis server.

configFields.label: Controller password
configFields.help: Auto-generated. Use this password for the web UI and controller API, including learning and configuration changes. Changing it requires a redeploy.

connection.title: Open Rspamd
connection.description: Sign in to the controller with the generated password. Connect your mail server to a private scan or milter worker.

guide.intro: Only the controller UI is routed publicly. HTTP scanning on port 11333 and milter on port 11332 stay on the project's private network.
guide.useHint: Use the controller password below; no username is required. Configure Redis separately for the features that need it.

outputs.label: HTTP scanner (private)
outputs.help: Use the normal worker's /checkv2 endpoint to scan messages on the private network.

outputs.label: Milter (private)
outputs.help: Connect your mail server's milter client to this private host and port.

features.title: Mail server integration
features.description: Use private HTTP scanning or milter with your existing mail server.

features.title: Controller access
features.description: Manage Rspamd with a generated password and a persistent data volume.

files.content:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
: "${RSPAMD_CONTROLLER_PASSWORD:?Controller password is required.}"
RSPAMD_CONTROLLER_PASSWORD_HASH="$(rspamadm pw --password "$RSPAMD_CONTROLLER_PASSWORD")"
case "$RSPAMD_CONTROLLER_PASSWORD_HASH" in
  '$2$'?*'$'?*) ;;
  *) echo 'Unable to hash the controller password.' >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
export RSPAMD_CONTROLLER_PASSWORD_HASH
unset RSPAMD_CONTROLLER_PASSWORD
exec /usr/bin/rspamd -f
